label: Lisbon and Porto
blurb: 10 days in April: tiled streets, river light, two cities by train.

brief.text: I want to photograph the tiled streets, trams and viewpoints of Lisbon, then take the train to Porto for the river and the bridges. I like working the old quarters by day and doing long exposures over the water at blue hour and after dark.

answer.title: Lisbon and Porto in spring
answer.summary: Six nights in Lisbon for viewpoints, trams and the Belém riverfront, with a morning at Pena Palace in Sintra, then the Alfa Pendular to Porto for azulejos, the Ribeira quay and the Dom Luís I Bridge. Sunsets go to west-facing viewpoints, and blue hour and night stops sit on the water for long exposures with the tripod and the six-stop ND.

spots.name: Senhora do Monte Viewpoint
spots.tip: Stand at the stone wall by the pine and frame the castle on the left with Baixa and the river beyond. Stay past sunset for the city lights coming on.

spots.name: Santa Justa Lift
spots.when: After dark, from the street below
spots.tip: Stand on Rua do Ouro at the foot of the lift and shoot up the lit iron tower with the 20mm. A two-second exposure turns a moving cabin into a soft streak.

spots.name: Jerónimos Monastery
spots.tip: Be at the door at opening and go straight to the two-storey cloister, shooting the carved arches from the corners of the upper gallery. Tripods are not allowed inside.

spots.name: MAAT
spots.localName: Museu de Arte, Arquitetura e Tecnologia
spots.tip: Walk up onto the curved roof and use the 85mm to line up its tiled curves with the 25 de Abril Bridge upriver.

spots.name: Belém Tower
spots.tip: Stand on the riverside path west of the tower so the low sun lights its carved face. At blue hour turn to the water with the six-stop ND for a smooth river.

spots.name: Santa Luzia Viewpoint
spots.when: Sunrise, over Alfama and the river
spots.tip: Use the azulejo panels and the pergola as foreground with Alfama's roofs and the river behind. At sunrise you have the terrace almost to yourself.

spots.name: Lisbon Cathedral and Tram 28
spots.tip: Stand uphill on Rua Augusto Rosa and wait for a yellow tram to round the bend in front of the cathedral towers. The 85mm compresses tram and facade together.

spots.name: Alfama lanes at Chafariz de Dentro
spots.tip: Start at the old fountain square and climb into Beco do Mexias and Rua de São Miguel for laundry lines, tiled doorways and neighbours on their steps. Work with the 35mm and ask before close portraits.

spots.name: Pena Palace
spots.tip: Take the train from Rossio to Sintra and the bus up, and shoot the red and yellow towers from the terraces before the tour groups arrive. The 85mm picks out the Moorish Castle on the next ridge.

spots.name: Cais das Colunas
spots.when: Blue hour, on the river steps
spots.tip: Set up on the steps between the two marble columns and use the six-stop ND to smooth the Tagus, with the 25 de Abril Bridge on the right horizon. Keep off the lowest steps when ferry wash comes in.

spots.name: Rua Augusta Arch
spots.tip: Stand in the middle of Praça do Comércio and shoot north through the floodlit arch, using the empty paving as foreground. The square thins out later in the evening.

spots.name: Feira da Ladra flea market
spots.tip: Walk the stalls of Campo de Santa Clara with the 35mm for traders, old tiles and bric-a-brac laid out on blankets. Go early, before the lanes between stalls fill up.

spots.name: National Pantheon
spots.tip: Climb to the terrace around the dome for a wide view over Alfama and the river, then shoot the marble floor from the gallery inside. Tripods are not allowed inside.

spots.name: São Pedro de Alcântara Viewpoint
spots.localName: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
spots.tip: Stand at the balustrade and shoot east across Baixa to the floodlit castle with the 85mm, keeping the railing out of the frame.

spots.name: Bica Funicular
spots.when: Morning, from the top of the street
spots.tip: Stand at the top by Largo do Calhariz and shoot down the steep street with the 85mm to stack the yellow car, the houses and a slice of river. Wait for the car to climb toward you.

spots.name: Carmo Convent ruins
spots.when: Midday, sky through the open nave
spots.tip: Shoot the roofless Gothic arches from the west end of the nave with the 20mm, letting the sky stand in for the vault. Closed on Sundays.

spots.name: Santa Catarina Viewpoint
spots.tip: Stand at the edge of the terrace by the Adamastor statue and frame the 25 de Abril Bridge over the river as the sun goes down to its right. The 85mm isolates the bridge and the Cristo Rei statue across the water.

spots.name: Glória Funicular
spots.tip: Stand on the stepped pavement halfway up Calçada da Glória and frame the yellow car against the painted walls as it passes. The cars run every few minutes, so you get plenty of attempts.

spots.name: Jardim do Morro
spots.tip: Stand at the top of the garden slope and frame the iron arch of the Dom Luís I Bridge with the Ribeira houses behind it in the last sun. Stay for blue hour as the bridge lights come on.

spots.name: São Bento Station
spots.tip: Stand at the back of the hall and shoot the blue and white azulejo panels with the 20mm, then use the 85mm to pick out single scenes. Keep the tripod packed in the busy hall.

spots.name: Carmo Church tiled wall
spots.tip: Cross to the far side of Rua do Carmo and fit the whole azulejo side wall in with the 20mm. Then step back to show the narrow house squeezed between Carmo and the Carmelitas church.

spots.name: Dom Luís I Bridge
spots.when: Blue hour, from the upper deck
spots.tip: Walk to the middle of the upper deck and shoot down over the Ribeira houses and the river as the lights come on. Metro trains share the deck, so time long exposures between them to avoid shake.

spots.name: Cais da Ribeira
spots.tip: Shoot along the quay with the stacked coloured houses on the left and the bridge closing the frame, before the cafe tables come out. The moored rabelo boats make a good foreground.

spots.name: Chapel of Souls
spots.tip: Stand across Rua de Santa Catarina and fit the tiled facade in at 20mm, then wait for a passer-by in front of the blue panels.

spots.name: Felgueiras Lighthouse
spots.tip: Set up on the promenade at the root of the breakwater and use the six-stop ND to smooth the swell around the small lighthouse as the sun drops into the Atlantic. Stay off the pier when waves break over it.

spots.name: Porto Cathedral terrace
spots.tip: Shoot the fortress-like facade from beside the pillory in the square, then turn to the terrace wall for the rooftops running down to the river.

spots.name: Vitória Viewpoint
spots.tip: Use the 85mm to compress the tiled roofs falling to the river against the port cellars of Gaia on the far bank. The cathedral sits on the ridge to your left.

spots.name: Ribeira from the Gaia riverfront
spots.tip: Set the tripod at the river wall opposite Praça da Ribeira and use a 20 to 30 second exposure to smooth the water under the lit houses, with the bridge on the right.

days.title: Arrival and first light over Lisbon

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: The highest viewpoint in the city gives a first sunset over the castle and Baixa.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: The lit iron lift is a short walk from the base and an easy first night subject.

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: The cloister is at its quietest in the first hour after opening.
slots.note: Closed on Mondays; tram 15 runs from Praça da Figueira.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.why: Clean modern lines and the bridge add an architecture frame between two heritage stops.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: The tower faces the estuary and takes warm side light in the last hour.

days.title: Alfama from sunrise to the lanes

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: Sunrise lights Alfama's roofs and the river from the tiled terrace.

slots.label: Midday
slots.why: Midday tram traffic on Rua Augusto Rosa gives plenty of chances at the classic street frame.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.why: The lanes below the viewpoint are a short walk downhill and quiet in the afternoon.

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: An early entry at Pena gets the palace terraces before the day crowds.
slots.note: Book a timed ticket in advance.

slots.label: Blue hour
slots.why: Back in the city, the columns and the river make the trip's first long exposure.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: The floodlit arch is steps from the river and the square empties after dinner.

days.title: Flea market, Pantheon and castle lights

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: Tuesday is market day, and the stalls give the trip's best street portraits.

slots.label: Midday
slots.why: The Pantheon is next to the market and its terrace gives a high view over Alfama.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: The floodlit castle across Baixa is the classic night view from Bairro Alto.

days.title: Chiado funiculars and a bridge sunset

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: The steep street is quiet in the morning and the funicular runs from early on.

slots.label: Midday
slots.why: High sun pours into the roofless nave, which suits the ruins.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: A west-facing terrace close to Bica, with the bridge and the river under the setting sun.

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: A short street session near Rossio before the train north.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: The first Porto evening goes to the classic view of Ribeira and the bridge from Gaia.

days.title: Azulejos and the bridge at blue hour

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: The station hall is next to the base and best before the midday tour groups.

slots.label: Midday
slots.why: Even midday light shows the tiled wall without hard shadows in the pattern.

slots.label: Blue hour
slots.why: The must-see bridge at blue hour, looking down on Ribeira as the lights come on.

days.title: Ribeira dawn and an Atlantic sunset

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: At dawn the quay is empty, hours before the cafe tables and the crowds arrive.

slots.label: Midday
slots.why: The tiled chapel suits flat midday light and sits on a busy shopping street.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: The coast faces west, so the sun sets straight into the sea behind the lighthouse.
slots.note: Bus 500 or tram 1 runs from the centre to Foz.

days.title: Cathedral, rooftops and Ribeira at night

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: Morning light on the terrace and the rooftops below the cathedral.

slots.label: Late afternoon
slots.why: Low sun warms the roofs between the viewpoint and the river.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: The last night closes with a long exposure of Ribeira lit across the river.

skipped.name: Quinta da Regaleira
skipped.reason: Sintra gets one morning, and Pena Palace is the stronger architecture subject.

skipped.name: Castelo de São Jorge
skipped.reason: The castle photographs better from Senhora do Monte and São Pedro de Alcântara than from inside its walls.

skipped.name: Livraria Lello
skipped.reason: Timed tickets and a packed interior make it a poor use of a camera morning.

skipped.name: Serra do Pilar Monastery viewpoint
skipped.reason: It repeats the Jardim do Morro view a short climb higher.
